---
title: "How to use this playbook"
description: "Who it is for, how it is organised, and how to find things quickly."
---

This playbook sets out how analysis is planned, produced, assured and communicated at NHSBSA.

## If you are in a hurry

Most people arrive with one question: **how much assurance does this piece of work need, and what do
I actually have to do?**

1. [Agree the question](../01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd) with
   your commissioner. The level is scored from it, so it comes first.
2. [Decide your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). Five minutes.
3. [Find what it requires](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). Read the column for your level.

That is the whole path. Everything else here exists for when you need it.

If you would rather see the whole route for your role before you start,
[journeys through this playbook](journeys.qmd) says where each one is, for the analyst, the commissioner, the
critical friend and the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. It also walks one Level 4 piece of
work through all four roles, so the routes can be read against one thing rather than in the
abstract.

## Who it is for

- **Commissioners** requesting analysis, including non-analysts and third-party suppliers
- **Analysts** producing it, and the **critical friends** assuring it
- **Analysis Senior Responsible Officers**, who approve one Business Critical output as fit for its
  intended use

## What it covers

**All of it.** NHSBSA takes an analytical output in the broadest sense: an output that results from
the collection, manipulation and interpretation of data to answer specific questions. That runs from a dataset created in answer to a Freedom of Information request or a Parliamentary
Question, through a sponsor's request for data to inform a policy decision. It takes in an official
statistics report and a dashboard for commissioners, up to a complex forecasting model informing
budgets. Used internally,
supplied to sponsors, or published externally: all of it is in scope.

Those are examples rather than a checklist, and there is no central record of everything NHSBSA
produces, so the test is the definition rather than the list. If you collected, manipulated or
interpreted data to answer a question, and somebody is going to act on the answer, this playbook
applies to it.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-does-it-apply.qmd >}}

What changes between them is how much assurance each one needs, and that is
[deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd). NHSBSA's own worked examples are there,
from exploratory analysis at Level 1 to a funding allocation formula at Level 4, along with the
eight types an analytical model can be.

## Find your kind of work

The playbook is organised by what you do, in the order you do it, and by who you are. Most people
arrive knowing neither of those and holding a piece of work. This is that way in.

**Where NHSBSA has placed each one is an example, not a ruling.** The placements come from the
decision sheet's own annex of worked examples, which is marked as still to be developed. Score your
own work in [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) rather than matching it to
the nearest row here.

| The work | Where NHSBSA has placed it | What else applies to it |
|------------------------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Exploratory analysis, an internal data investigation | Level 1 Standard | Level 1 is not "no assurance". It is separation within your team, and [deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) says what that means |
| A monthly operational dashboard, team workforce planning | Level 2 Enhanced | It runs again, so [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd) is as relevant as [the checks, by level](/guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd#the-checks-by-level): what a recurring output is reviewed against, and when |
| An official statistics publication, such as Prescription Cost Analysis or Dental Statistics | Level 3 Comprehensive | The Code of Practice, in [ethics and transparency](../09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd). For advice on official statistics, the Head of Profession for Statistics, [who to ask](../09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd) |
| An FOI response or a Parliamentary Question | Level 3 Comprehensive | Visibility is scored under public visibility and reach rather than added on top. [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) draws the route, including what to do when there is not time |
| A Board report or a ministerial briefing | Level 3 Comprehensive | High visibility raises how much assurance the work needs. On its own it does not make the analysis Business Critical |
| A funding allocation formula, an eligibility model, a payment methodology, a major policy appraisal | Level 4 Business Critical | [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd) is the whole route in nine steps. The register entry and the named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer are settled at scoping, not at delivery |
| A dataset supplied to a sponsor or a partner | Score it like any other analysis | Supplied externally rather than published is still in scope, as the paragraph above says |
| A forecasting model informing budgets | Score it, then place it among the eight model types | [Deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) for both, and [uncertainty, assumptions and limitations](../09-resources/r10-uncertainty.qmd), because what the model does not know is most of what the reader needs |
| An algorithmic or machine learning tool that affects decisions about people | Score it, and separately check transparency scope | Two decisions, settled by different things, both at scoping. [Ethics and transparency](../09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) carries the test |
| An AI assistant helping you write code, summarise or draft | Nothing changes about who is accountable | Different from the row above, which is analysis **of** an algorithmic tool. [Ethics and transparency](../09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd) has the five rules, and they are short |
| Analysis you are reusing for a new purpose, or a one-off that has become a monthly production run | The original's assurance may no longer hold | [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd): four things to check before the reuse.<br><br>A one-off that becomes a production run is a different piece of work, and reuse is the usual reason to change a level |
| A published figure that has turned out to be wrong | Not a new piece of analysis | [Phase 4, delivery and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd): first whether it is a revision or a correction, then the grade by consequence |
| Work where there is not enough time for the assurance the level asks | The level does not change | [After you have your level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/after-you-have-your-level.qmd): narrow the question, or state plainly what assurance was not done |

## How it is organised

**Five phases and four roles.** The five phases are the shape of the work, and the sidebar runs
them in the order the work happens. The four roles run across all five phases, and each role has a
page saying what is theirs in each. Everything you look up while working sits in the toolkit, and
the principles, the standards and the definitions sit in Resources.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-lifecycle.qmd >}}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-playbook-map.qmd >}}

{{< include /guidance/_partials/section-contents.qmd >}}

Business Critical analysis gathers rather than adds. Being Business Critical changes what happens
at seven points across the five phases, and that page puts them in the order you meet them.

## Giving feedback

This playbook is maintained and it is meant to change. If something here is wrong, unclear, or does
not match how work actually happens, say so. [Who to ask](../09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.qmd) has the
route.
